decisive_items: cystic lesion in the uncinate process with a smooth-walled capsule containing calcifications, enhancing septa, millimetric nodules, and soft-tissue components
complex cystic mass in the pancreatic head measuring 5.5 × 4.5 cm with internal calcifications and mural nodularity
complex cystic mass in the pancreatic head
response.rationale: IPMN is favored by an elderly woman with a complex cystic pancreatic head/uncinate lesion showing enhancing septa, mural nodules, and soft-tissue components; MCN classically affects the pancreatic tail, SPN typically younger patients, serous cystadenoma lacks enhancing mural nodules, and pancreatic cancer is usually solid.

rejected.why: Shares cystic complexity, calcifications, and septa but MCN is classically located in the pancreatic body/tail, not the uncinate process.
Serous cystadenoma may have smooth walls and calcifications but typically lacks enhancing mural nodules and soft-tissue components.
SPN often has capsule, calcifications, and solid components but usually occurs in younger women and is less characteristic in the uncinate process at this age.
Pancreatic cancer is typically a solid mass; this is a complex cystic lesion without obstruction-related symptoms, and prior breast cancer alone does not establish pancreatic metastasis or carcinoma.
